body.Session Title: Network Type Identification and Component Assembly
body.Session Topic Hints:
NETWORK TYPE DETERMINATION

- Analyzing network design documents to identify required network types (LAN, WAN, etc.)

- Matching business needs with appropriate network architectures

COMPONENT & MEDIA ASSEMBLY FOR LAN

- Selecting appropriate switches, routers, and cabling for a LAN

- Physical assembly and connection of LAN components
body.LP Outcomes and Key Points:
Outcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:

a. Identify appropriate network types based on design specifications.

b. Assemble prerequisite components and media for specific network types.
Key Points: NETWORK TYPE DETERMINATION

- Analyzing network design documents to identify required network types (LAN, WAN, etc.)

- Matching business needs with appropriate network architectures

COMPONENT & MEDIA ASSEMBLY FOR LAN

- Selecting appropriate switches, routers, and cabling for a LAN

- Physical assembly and connection of LAN components
Activities: - Work through Case Studies to identify appropriate network types for different organizational needs.

- Engage in Demonstrations with Participation to assemble prerequisite components and media for a given LAN scenario.

- Participate in a Group Discussion to explain the selection criteria for network components for a WAN.

Follow up Activity:

1. Given a new office layout, propose a network type and list all necessary components and media for its implementation. (10 Marks)

Due date:

json.Session Title: Introduction to Network Security and Threats
json.Session Topic Hints:
Session 1 Key Points:
NETWORK SECURITY DEFINITION

- Definition of network security and its core principles (confidentiality, integrity, availability)

- Importance of securing network infrastructure

INTERNAL NETWORK THREATS

- Insider threats (e.g., disgruntled employees, accidental data leakage)

- Misconfigurations and weak passwords within the network

Session 2 Key Points:
INTERNAL NETWORK THREATS

- Insider threats (e.g., disgruntled employees, accidental data leakage)

- Misconfigurations and weak passwords within the network

EXTERNAL NETWORK THREATS

- Malware (viruses, worms, ransomware), phishing attacks

- Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, brute-force attacks
json.LP Outcomes and Key Points:
Session 1 Outcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:

a. Define network security and its objectives.

b. Identify common internal and external network threats.
Session 1 Key Points: NETWORK SECURITY DEFINITION

- Definition of network security and its core principles (confidentiality, integrity, availability)

- Importance of securing network infrastructure

INTERNAL NETWORK THREATS

- Insider threats (e.g., disgruntled employees, accidental data leakage)

- Misconfigurations and weak passwords within the network
Session 1 Activities: - Engage in a Think-Pair-Share activity to define network security and its importance.

- Participate in a Brainstorming session to identify common internal and external network threats.

- Work through Case Studies on recent cyberattacks to explain the impact of various network threats.

Follow up Activity:

1. Research a significant cyberattack incident from the last year and summarize its nature, impact, and lessons learned. (10 Marks)
